alt: A detailed view of the formal HHS OCR HIPAA complaint form filed against Palmdale Regional Medical Center on June 21, 2026.
summary: This document is the redacted filing form of the formal administrative complaint submitted to the HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) against Palmdale Regional Medical Center. It outlines violations of 45 C.F.R. § 164.526(b) for failure to timely act on a PHI records amendment request and failure to provide a written notice of extension within the statutory 60-day window, documenting carrier-level fax failure receipts for (661) 382-5011 and (661) 382-5056 alongside successful delivery confirmation to (661) 382-5499.
full_text:
I am filing this complaint against Palmdale Regional Medical Center for failing to respond to my formal request to amend my protected health information (PHI) within the 60-day statutory period required under 45 C.F.R. § 164.526(b), and for failing to provide any written notice of extension as permitted under that same provision.

On April 20, 2026, I submitted a formal written request to amend my medical record, pursuant to 45 C.F.R. § 164.526, to Palmdale Regional Medical Center. Although the request document itself was addressed to the primary medical records fax line at (661) 382-5011, repeated transmission attempts to both that line and the alternate Medical Records fax line at (661) 382-5056 failed due to carrier/hardware errors on the hospital's end (confirmed by the enclosed failure reports). Consequently, the document was successfully transmitted to and received by the facility's published secure provider fax gateway at (661) 382-5499 on April 20, 2026, at 17:48 PDT. Third-party transmission logs confirming successful, page-by-page delivery to this alternate number are enclosed.

The request concerned my Emergency Department visit on December 6, 2025 (MRN: PRM10252427, FIN: PRM0003016618153). The visit record lists the diagnosis as "Medication refill; Substance abuse." I requested that the "Substance abuse" marker be removed, as it is clinically unsupported. The clinical record contains no diagnostic findings, physical evaluations, toxicologies, or laboratory testing to support a substance abuse diagnosis. I presented solely to obtain an emergency medication refill, and the only intervention documented or provided was a 3-day bridge prescription for buprenorphine-naloxone (Suboxone) due to a pharmacy delay. The mismatch between the diagnosis entered and the actual clinical treatment rendered demonstrates the diagnosis does not reflect the clinical reality of the visit.

Under 45 C.F.R. § 164.526(b), the covered entity was required to act on my request — by accepting, denying, or requesting a one-time 30-day extension in writing — no later than 60 days from receipt, which was June 19, 2026.

As of the date of this complaint, I have received absolutely no communication from Palmdale Regional Medical Center: no acceptance, no denial, no written extension notice, and no acknowledgment of receipt.

I am alleging that Palmdale Regional Medical Center violated 45 C.F.R. § 164.526(b) by failing to timely act on my amendment request and failing to provide any written notice of extension within the required timeframe. I respectfully request that OCR investigate this systemic default and take appropriate action to ensure Palmdale Regional Medical Center complies with its federal obligations, including providing an immediate substantive response to my pending amendment request.
